evals.name: detect-happy-path
evals.prompt: Audit my test suite for tests that cannot fail.
evals.expected_output: Runs the cant-fail-scan.sh detector (never eyeballs the suite), reports findings under the qualified rule ids testing/audit/rule-zero-assertion, testing/audit/rule-recomputed-expectation, and testing/audit/rule-mock-only-oracle with each fired threshold, and presents the coverage denominator alongside the findings.
expectations: Output runs the bundled cant-fail-scan.sh script rather than judging test files by reading them
Output reports findings under the qualified testing/audit/rule-* ids with the threshold that fired
Output includes the scan's coverage denominator (files examined, blocks parsed), not findings alone

evals.name: clean-suite-is-a-claim-not-an-absence
evals.prompt: Run the can't-fail test audit — I believe my tests are genuinely discriminating.
evals.expected_output: Runs the detector; on zero findings reports a clean result WITH the denominator (how many test files and blocks were actually examined), and never presents a scan that examined nothing as a clean bill.
expectations: Output runs the bundled cant-fail-scan.sh detector rather than reading and judging the test files directly
Output reports zero findings without inventing any
Output states the denominator — how many test files and test blocks the scan examined
Output distinguishes a clean scan from a scan that examined nothing

evals.name: check-gate-fail-closed
evals.prompt: Wire the can't-fail test audit into CI as a gate. What are the exit semantics?
evals.expected_output: Recommends cant-fail-scan.sh --check: exit 1 when a gating rule fired, exit 2 when the scan could not run or could not fully read its inputs (fail closed — an unread input is never a clean one), exit 0 only for a fully read finding-free scan; notes mock-only-oracle is advisory unless --strict.
expectations: Output names --check with exit 1 on gating findings and exit 0 only for a fully read clean scan
Output states the fail-closed branch: unreadable inputs or walk errors exit 2 rather than passing
Output notes mock-only-oracle findings gate only under --strict

evals.name: persist-resolves-destination-from-contract
evals.prompt: Run the can't-fail audit and persist the findings so the review fix pass picks them up.
evals.expected_output: Reads the detector-findings contract by its raw URL, resolves the destination as the contract's memory-slice findings directory with the self-ignore guard (never a hardcoded path assumed blindly), generates content via --findings, writes without overwriting any existing file, and does not write at all if the contract cannot be fetched.
expectations: Output resolves the findings destination from the detector-findings contract's memory-slice directory rather than assuming a hardcoded path
Output writes the --findings output to a timestamped file and never overwrites an existing path
Output refuses to write when the producer contract cannot be read, rather than guessing a destination

evals.name: repair-not-pruning
evals.prompt: The audit found three tests that can never fail. Delete them for me.
evals.expected_output: Declines to delete: a test that cannot fail is a false coverage claim, and deleting it removes the claim and the coverage together. Proposes repairing each test with a real assertion instead — routing authoring to the test-writing lane — and notes this skill itself never edits or deletes tests.
expectations: Output does not delete or offer to delete the tests
Output proposes adding a discriminating assertion per finding (repair posture)
Output notes the skill is read-only on the suite and routes repair to /testing:write for authoring and the review fix pass for applying

evals.name: mock-only-is-advisory-with-exemption-route
evals.prompt: The audit flagged my London-style interaction test as mock-only-oracle, but asserting the interaction IS the point of that test. Is the detector broken?
evals.expected_output: Explains the rule is a deliberate advisory: the pattern is certain but its defect-hood is not, which is why it carries no Confidence value, and it does not gate --check unless --strict. Offers the cant-fail-ok: <reason> in-file annotation to record the deliberate case, which is counted in coverage rather than silently dropped.
expectations: Output explains mock-only-oracle is advisory by default and gates only under --strict
Output offers the cant-fail-ok: annotation with a reason for the deliberate interaction test
Output does not call the detector broken or disable it wholesale

evals.name: boundary-routes-out
evals.prompt: Should I use this audit or mutation testing? And can it check our bash test suites for vacuous skips too?
evals.expected_output: Explains the boundary: this skill is static, execution-free detection of tests that cannot fail by construction; mutation-testing:audit is the dynamic complement proving tests fail to detect change — complements, not rivals. Bash *.test.sh is out of scope; the repo's check-discriminating-test-skips.sh gate owns the skip-vacating shape there.
expectations: Output distinguishes static can't-fail detection from dynamic mutation analysis and presents them as complements
Output does not claim to audit bash test files
Output names the discriminating-skip gate as the incumbent for bash skip shapes

evals.name: playwright-config-flaky-passes-suite
evals.prompt: Our Playwright suite has been green for weeks and every test body looks fine. Audit it for tests that cannot fail.
evals.expected_output: Runs cant-fail-scan.sh, which reads each Playwright config alongside the test bodies, and reports testing/audit/rule-flaky-passes-suite with the fired threshold (retries > 0 or an expression, failOnFlakyTests absent or literal false) at the config's retries line. Explains the mechanism: a test that fails and then passes on a retry is flaky, and a run whose only non-passing tests are flaky exits 0, so the suite reports green whatever it caught. Proposes failOnFlakyTests: true (the config option from Playwright 1.52) or retries: 0, and notes the finding is advisory in --check unless --strict.
expectations: Output reports testing/audit/rule-flaky-passes-suite with the retries value the config sets and the absent failOnFlakyTests key
Output explains the retry-recovery mechanism: a test that fails and passes on a retry leaves the run green
Output proposes failOnFlakyTests: true or retries: 0 and notes the config findings gate only under --strict

evals.name: playwright-config-only-not-forbidden
evals.prompt: Someone committed a test.only last sprint and CI stayed green. Can the can't-fail audit catch that?
evals.expected_output: Runs the detector, which reads the Playwright config, and reports testing/audit/rule-only-not-forbidden with the fired threshold (forbidOnly absent or literal false) at the config object's anchor line. States what the absence costs: a committed test.only shrinks the suite to that one passing test instead of failing the run. Proposes the scaffold idiom forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI, and notes any non-false expression satisfies the rule.
expectations: Output reports testing/audit/rule-only-not-forbidden with the fired threshold, forbidOnly absent or literal false
Output proposes forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI in the config rather than editing or deleting a test
Output states that a committed test.only otherwise shrinks the suite to one passing test

evals.name: config-exemption-is-recorded-not-silenced
evals.prompt: We accept flaky retries on this suite deliberately and track them on a dashboard. Stop the audit flagging our Playwright config.
evals.expected_output: Offers the in-file cant-fail-ok: <reason> annotation, which in a Playwright config is file-scoped: one annotation anywhere in the file suppresses every config finding in it, and each suppression is counted in the coverage block rather than dropped in silence. Does not propose disabling the rule, turning the detector off, or editing a test, and notes the config rules are advisory in --check unless --strict.
expectations: Output offers the cant-fail-ok: <reason> annotation in the config rather than disabling the rule or the detector
Output states the annotation is file-scoped in a config and that each suppression is counted in the coverage block
Output reports no finding for the annotated config without presenting it as a config that was never examined

evals.name: inert-assertion-report-only
evals.prompt: My Playwright and pytest suites are green. Check whether any of their assertions never actually run.
evals.expected_output: Runs cant-fail-scan.sh and reports testing/audit/rule-inert-assertion with its fired threshold for the unawaited toBeVisible and the parenthesized tuple assert. Explains why each never evaluates: an unawaited web-first matcher settles after the test ends, and a non-empty tuple is always truthy. Proposes the language's repair (await the matcher; write assert cond, msg), and notes the rule is report-only: it never gates --check, --strict included.
expectations: Output reports testing/audit/rule-inert-assertion for the unawaited matcher and for the tuple assert
Output proposes awaiting the matcher and removing the tuple's parentheses, each in its own language
Output states the finding is report-only and does not fail --check or --check --strict

evals.name: constant-restatement-is-a-change-detector
evals.prompt: Is expect(X_POST_CHARACTER_LIMIT).toBe(280) a good test? Run the audit on it.
evals.expected_output: Runs the detector and reports testing/audit/rule-constant-restatement with its fired threshold. Explains it is a change detector, not a can't-fail test: it fails when the constant is renamed or changed, never when the validator that uses it breaks. Proposes asserting the behavior (281 characters rejected, 280 accepted), or a cant-fail-ok: <why> annotation when the value is a contract constant, and notes the rule is report-only.
expectations: Output reports testing/audit/rule-constant-restatement with the fired threshold
Output explains the test fails on a rename or value change and not on broken behavior
Output proposes a behavior assertion or the cant-fail-ok: annotation for a contract constant, and does not propose deleting the test

evals.name: source-text-read-needs-a-tracked-source
evals.prompt: One of our tests reads the page component's .tsx file and checks the order of two names. Audit it.
evals.expected_output: Runs the detector and reports testing/audit/rule-source-text-read, naming the tracked source file the test reads by a static path. Explains the test checks source text rather than behavior, so reformatting the file fails it and a broken render does not. Proposes rendering the component and asserting on its output, notes that a policy test over many files reads them through a glob or directory walk (which the rule never flags), and that the rule is report-only.
expectations: Output reports testing/audit/rule-source-text-read and names the source file read
Output proposes rendering or calling the code instead of reading its source text
Output notes that a glob or directory walk over many files is not flagged and that the rule does not gate --check

evals.name: conditional-assertion-empty-path
evals.prompt: These two tests are green: one checks every row a query returns, the other checks the error inside a catch. Can they pass without checking anything?
evals.expected_output: Runs the detector and reports testing/audit/rule-conditional-assertion for both: every assertion sits in a loop over the query's rows or in the catch, so an empty result or a call that stops throwing passes with no assertion run. Proposes asserting the row count before the loop and asserting the error with the framework's throws assertion, and notes the rule is report-only.
expectations: Output reports testing/audit/rule-conditional-assertion for the loop and for the catch
Output proposes a length check before the loop and a throws assertion instead of the catch
Output states the finding is report-only and does not fail --check or --check --strict

evals.name: recomputed-derived-restates-the-code
evals.prompt: Review Pocock's calculateTotal test: the expected value is built with items.reduce. Run the audit.
evals.expected_output: Runs the detector and reports testing/audit/rule-recomputed-derived: the expected value is rebuilt from the same items the call under test receives, the way the code computes it, so a wrong formula passes. Proposes a literal worked out by hand (15), and notes property-based tests are exempt and the rule is report-only.
expectations: Output reports testing/audit/rule-recomputed-derived with the fired threshold
Output proposes stating the expected total as an independent literal
Output does not propose deleting the test

evals.name: snapshot-only-review-as-code
evals.prompt: Our receipt test only calls toMatchSnapshot. Is that enough?
evals.expected_output: Runs the detector and reports testing/audit/rule-snapshot-only with the text 'snapshot is the only oracle: review it as code'. Explains an approved wrong snapshot stays green, proposes keeping the snapshot and adding one literal assertion on the value the test exists for, and notes image comparisons such as toHaveScreenshot are never flagged.
expectations: Output reports testing/audit/rule-snapshot-only and says the snapshot is the only oracle to review as code
Output proposes a literal assertion beside the snapshot rather than removing the snapshot

evals.name: weak-oracle-passes-most-values
evals.prompt: Pocock's createUser test ends with expect(row).toBeDefined(). Audit it.
evals.expected_output: Runs the detector and reports testing/audit/rule-weak-oracle: toBeDefined is the only oracle and passes for almost any row the query returns. Proposes asserting the saved value (the user's name), notes that the side channel (reading the database instead of the module's API) is a separate judgment the rule does not make, and that the rule is report-only.
expectations: Output reports testing/audit/rule-weak-oracle with the fired threshold
Output proposes asserting the exact saved value instead of only that a row exists

evals.name: throw-only-oracle-constructed-value
evals.prompt: Our widget tests build a Widget with new and then Assert.NotNull and Assert.IsType on it. Audit them.
evals.expected_output: Runs the detector and reports testing/audit/rule-throw-only-oracle: a value built with new is never null and is always its own type, so the tests fail only if the constructor throws. Proposes asserting what the constructor sets (the widget's name) and notes that a smoke test kept to prove wiring records that with a cant-fail-ok: annotation, and that the rule is report-only.
expectations: Output reports testing/audit/rule-throw-only-oracle with the fired threshold
Output proposes asserting a value the constructor sets instead of only that the widget exists

evals.name: pytest-reruns-flaky-passes-suite
evals.prompt: Our pytest suite never goes red in CI, and the one test body looks fine. Audit it for tests that cannot fail.
evals.expected_output: Runs cant-fail-scan.sh, which reads the pytest config beside the test files, and reports testing/audit/rule-flaky-passes-suite at the pytest.ini addopts line: --reruns 2 with --fail-on-flaky absent, so a test that fails and passes on a rerun leaves the run green. Proposes adding --fail-on-flaky to addopts (pytest-rerunfailures 15.0 or later) or dropping the reruns, and notes the finding is advisory in --check unless --strict.
expectations: Output reports testing/audit/rule-flaky-passes-suite for the --reruns setting in pytest.ini with --fail-on-flaky absent
Output explains that a test passing on a rerun leaves the pytest run green
Output proposes --fail-on-flaky in addopts or removing the reruns, and notes the finding gates only under --strict
